projects.title: Birds
projects.description:
[Gumroad](https://aylesim.gumroad.com/l/birds) · [Isotonik Studios](https://isotonikstudios.com/product/birds-by-alessandro-aylesim-miracapillo/)

## Overview

Birds is a generative MIDI sequencer for Ableton Live, built as a Max for Live device. It takes a short MIDI phrase and rewrites it in real time, with enough of the original structure left that the result stays usable.

![Birds - Max for Live interface](/Birdsgr.png)

The interface is an animated score: each bird is a note, the wire is pitch, horizontal position is timing. Making that readable was as much of the work as the sequencer logic.

## How it works

A **Difference Limit** measures how far each new generation can move from a reference pattern. Pitch, rhythm, density, and register can shift, but only within a set distance from the source. Variation is a bounded rewrite, not a random scramble.

- **Rule-based melodic generation** with different strategies for rewriting source material
- **Real-time pitch and rhythm mutation** with controls for gate behavior and instability
- **Scale-aware and chromatic modes** for different harmonic constraints
- **Density and range controls** for both musical output and how the system responds
- **Transport-driven or MIDI-triggered playback** for studio and performance use
highlights: Rule-based generative system for melodic variation inside Max for Live
Visual mapping where pitch, timing, and note state stay readable while the sequence changes
Difference Limit model keeps algorithmic output inside musical bounds

projects.title: Planetary Compendium
projects.description:
## Overview

Planetary Compendium is a web platform made with the Berggruen Institute and Dark Matter Labs. It collects case studies on planetary governance: how institutions, infrastructures, and local experiments try to organise life at Earth scale.

The public site is [governtheplanet.org](https://governtheplanet.org/). Visitors move through long-form case studies with scrollytelling, spatial layouts, and audio.

![Planetary Compendium - interface](/planetary.png)

## What the platform does

- Case studies on planetary governance in long-form editorial pages
- Themes include sovereignty, shared vulnerability, ecology, and more-than-human agency
- Spatial navigation across related concepts
- Used in live workshops; the pages stay stable with a group on the same view

## My contribution

I was a freelance web developer from May to November 2025, remote, in a mixed team. I built:

- **Scrollytelling interfaces**: narrative sequences tied to content and visual transitions
- **Spatial data exploration**: layouts for related concepts and case studies
- **Audio-driven narratives**: sound layers on editorial pages
- **Content modules** for dense text and media
- **Accessibility**, including reduced-motion paths, from the first release

## Context and outcome

The Compendium launched in November 2025 with a virtual event and a physical exhibition in Zürich. It is a public publication, also used in workshops.

> "The Planetary Compendium serves to entangle not only what the Planetary could be but how it is already manifesting regionally and disciplinarily."  
> - Zehra Zaidi OBE, Mission Lead for Planetary Civics, Dark Matter Labs
highlights: Prix Ars Electronica 2026 — Honorary Mention, Digital Humanity
Scrollytelling and spatial data exploration
Audio-driven narrative interfaces
Reduced-motion and other accessibility paths from the first release
Stable rendering during live group sessions and public exhibition

projects.title: Max Berlin Network
projects.description:
## Overview

[Max Berlin Network](https://www.maxberlin.network/) is the website I co-founded and built in early **2025** for a Berlin-based Max/MSP network. The job is narrow: when the next session is, where it happens, how to get on the list, and where to read about past meetups, without relying on scattered social posts.

![Max Berlin Network homepage](/max-berlin-network.png)

The visual language is poster-like: bold type, slight rotations, monospace detail. The layout puts date, venue, and signup first.

## What the site does

- **Next meetup** on the homepage with date, venue, time, and a link to the full event page
- **Newsletter** capture for upcoming meetups, open calls, and announcements
- **Meetup archive** for past sessions
- **About**, plus outbound links to Discord and Instagram
- **Light / dark** theme toggle

## My contribution

I shaped the information architecture and built the site in **Next.js** and **TypeScript**, deployed on **Vercel**. Meetup copy and scheduling stay editable without treating the homepage as a one-off static file.

- **Event routing**: a page per meetup with a stable URL
- **Homepage data**: next session pulled into the hero so the primary call to action stays current
- **Newsletter flow**: signup in the main layout
- **Share metadata**: Open Graph and Twitter cards for link previews
highlights: Designed and built the public site at maxberlin.network
Homepage shows next meetup date, venue, and detail pages without a redeploy for every edit
Newsletter signup and social links between sessions
Meetup archive and about pages for past events and the initiative

projects.title: Knob Studio
projects.description:
[Gumroad](https://aylesim.gumroad.com/l/knobstudio) · [Isotonik Studios](https://isotonikstudios.com/product/knob-studio-by-alessandro-aylesim-miracapillo/) · [Attack Magazine Store](https://store.attackmagazine.com/products/knob-studio)

## Overview

Knob Studio is a Max for Live audio effect for parameter modulation in Ableton Live. Several layers can run in parallel, hit the same targets, and stay editable.

![Knob Studio - Max for Live interface](/knobstudio.png)

The device is a waveform-driven modulation graph: functions are stacked, shaped, then read under different strategies. The graph is meant to stay readable while it runs.

## How it works

Stacked waveform functions, each with its own parameters, are interpreted by **reading heads**. Heads can be driven by hand, by LFOs, or by an envelope follower, which changes how the same material is scanned over time.

Randomization adjusts parameters within fixed limits. Global smoothing and jitter keep the whole modulator field moving together when you want cohesion.

- **Layered function stack** for building modulation shapes from simpler pieces
- **Multiple head modes**: manual control, periodic motion, audio-responsive scanning
- **Real-time waveform display** aligned with what is being applied to parameters
- **Randomization** with clear entry points so exploration does not erase the starting point
- **Global smoothing and jitter** across active modulations
highlights: Covered by Rekkerd and Attack Magazine on release
Featured in Attack Magazine’s long-read on Max for Live modulation
Layered modulation engine with multiple concurrent function generators
Reading-head modes (manual, LFO, envelope follower) on shared waveform material
Real-time visualization tied to the modulation being applied
Randomization plus global smoothing and jitter as macros over the modulator field

projects.title: Disco
projects.description:
[Gumroad](https://aylesim.gumroad.com/l/disco) · [Isotonik Studios](https://isotonikstudios.com/product/disco-by-aylsim/)

## Overview

Disco is a Max for Live audio effect built around a circular multi-tap delay. Incoming audio is spread across several delay lines whose positions can rotate on a ring, together or independently, so repeats bunch, spread, and re-phase over time. Time-domain DSP, Euclidean pattern logic, and the Live interface all had to hold together.

![Disco - Max for Live interface](/disco.png)

The delay is a small moving system of timed events, not a single feedback line. The interface has to stay readable while it shifts, so you can see where rhythmic density and stereo energy are accumulating.

## How it works

Each tap is a point on a cycle. Position sets time offset around the ring. Gain and pan place that tap in the mix. Rotation re-phases taps relative to the input. Manual control or LFO-driven motion changes the angular velocity of the whole structure or of individual steps, which produces the acceleration and deceleration in the repeats.

- **Multi-tap delay bank** with Euclidean-style spacing as a starting geometry, not a fixed preset
- **Per-step parameters** for level, stereo placement, and bypass
- **Coupled or decoupled rotation** so taps move as one field or drift against each other
- **LFO and manual modulation** of spin rate for sweeps and static geometries
highlights: Multi-tap delay engine in Max for Live with per-step gain, pan, and on/off in a circular layout
Independent or ganged rotation of delay taps for Euclidean-style patterns and spin effects
Manual control and LFO-driven motion, from small movement to extreme modulation
UI built around a spatial readout of time and level so delay density stays readable while taps move

projects.title: Freesound4Live
projects.description:
Currently not available.

## Overview

Freesound4Live is a free Max for Live utility I built to browse [Freesound.org](https://freesound.org/) from inside Ableton Live. You search, audition, and pull samples into the session without leaving Live for a browser. The patch respects Max UI limits and Live’s rules for where sample files may land.

![Freesound4Live - Max for Live interface](/ffl.png)

Freesound is treated as a remote catalog with strict metadata. License and duration stay visible, because they matter when you import audio into a project that might be published.

## How it works

Search requests are parameterized (text, tags, duration bounds, license filters). Responses become a compact list for in-device preview. Previews stream before anything is written to disk. On confirm, audio drops onto Drum Rack pads or into Simpler without a separate file-management step.

- **Query and filter** on Freesound’s fields so long result lists can be scanned
- **Preview before download** so network use stays predictable in a session or class
- **License-aware browsing** so CC and other terms are visible at selection time
- **Live-native placement** via drag-and-drop into rack and sampler slots
highlights: Featured on Create Digital Music for bringing the Freesound.org library into Ableton Live
Filters by tag, duration, and license metadata
Drag-and-drop into Drum Rack and Simpler
Released as open source

projects.title: Lucky Notes
projects.description:
[Gumroad](https://aylesim.gumroad.com/l/luckynotes)

## Overview

Lucky Notes is a small Max for Live MIDI effect. It passes or drops incoming notes according to a single probability control, so you can thin a busy clip or bring a pattern toward full density from the device instead of duplicating clips or drawing automation. I use it most after a mono sequencer on melodic material. It also behaves predictably on rhythmic parts.

![Lucky Notes - Max for Live interface](/LN.png)

At 0% probability the lane stays effectively silent. At 100% every note is let through. Between those extremes the stream thins or thickens in real time, which is useful for rehearsing builds without rewriting MIDI.

The Gumroad page is free. It has **more than two thousand downloads**.

## How it works

The device sits on a MIDI track in front of an instrument. Each note-on is evaluated against the current probability threshold, with randomization so the result is musical rather than a fixed skip pattern. There is no audio path. The patch only decides which notes fire, which keeps CPU low.

- **Single main control** for probability, meant for live adjustment
- **MIDI-only processing** so it stays light in large sets
- **Typical Live chains**: before instruments, after sequencers

I implemented MIDI note gating, probability scaling, and a UI that stays legible under stage lighting.
highlights: Listed in the ELPHNT Max for Live Curated Collection
MIDI effect that gates notes by probability for live arrangement
Control range lets patterns start sparse and grow denser without extra clip editing
Free Gumroad download, more than two thousand downloads

projects.title: Please Set a Password
projects.description:
## Overview

Please Set a Password is an audio-visual installation about mass surveillance and personal responsibility online. Private and semi-private spaces become visible when camera software is left open to the network, and that exposure is now ordinary.

The title reads like a forgotten default prompt. It is also a direct request to anyone who installs or maintains these systems: actually secure them.
projects.descriptionAfterVideos:
## How it works

A custom process searches the public internet for hosts serving the web interfaces of unsecured surveillance cameras, then pulls and displays their feeds in real time. What appears on screen is not staged footage. It is live material from cameras reachable without authentication.

Sound is generated in real time through audio synthesis shaped by image analysis of the video stream, so timbre and density follow the image.

The pipeline has to run continuously in a room. Some feeds are not shown.

## Recognition

First place in Electronic Arts at the Italian National Arts Award XV (Premio Nazionale delle Arti Italiane), Sassari, Italy.
highlights: Locates IP addresses exposing unsecured surveillance-camera interfaces and aggregates their live feeds for projection
Real-time audio synthesis driven by analysis of the incoming imagery
Italian National Arts Award XV - first place, Electronic Arts (Sassari, Italy)

projects.title: There Will Be No More Determination
projects.description:
## Overview

There Will Be No More Determination is about military imaging technology and what it does to the people caught in its frame. Generative adversarial networks (GANs) rework helicopter footage from conflict zones into abstract images. The source still reads as “war vision” from above. The model’s output is harder to pin down: flattened, slightly wrong, difficult to read as either document or abstraction.

The title refers to Éléonore Weber’s documentary *There Will Be No More Night* (with Nathalie Richard). The reference is a shared question about agency, not an illustration of the film: what happens to determination, orientation, and care when sight is weaponised and bodies become coordinates.
projects.descriptionAfterVideos:
## How it works

The core is a GAN pipeline trained on military helicopter video from Afghanistan, Iraq, Pakistan, and comparable contexts. The network learns patterns in that material, then generates images that inherit its textures and motion without producing a clean scene. The output drifts away from identifiable scenes. The training material is the same kind of aerial footage used to manage violence at a distance.

The work included dataset limits, training, and how the outputs should sit in a room: how many images, at what scale, how quickly a viewer should go from looking at a picture to recognising the source.

## Context

Developed during Con.divisione Residenza 2022 in Maul.
highlights: GANs trained on military helicopter footage from conflict zones, including Afghanistan, Iraq, and Pakistan
Abstract images that still read as aerial war vision, aimed at the distance built into military imaging
Residency: Con.divisione Residenza 2022 - Maul

projects.title: Wikyslavery
projects.description:
## Overview

Wikyslavery is a net art installation that automates misleading edits to unspecified Wikipedia articles. It treats Wikipedia as infrastructure and as a cultural symbol. Real-time processes keep altered text in circulation long enough that Wikipedia’s social machinery shows: patrol workflows, revert speed, and the unpaid attention that holds the encyclopaedia together.

The piece occupies time that would otherwise go to ordinary maintenance, and makes that cost explicit. It also asks what counts as a stable source when content can be automated, and who pays when it is not.
projects.descriptionAfterVideos:
## How it works

Algorithms run continuously, selecting targets and mutating text that is coherent enough to pass a quick scan, then still triggers correction. Wikipedia is framed as a public record and as training data for large models. If machine learning systems ingest the open web, small distributed distortions can look authoritative because of the channel they arrive through, while still costing human editors time.

The title joins wiki and slavery on purpose. It names a loop where human attention is extracted to repair what machines and scripts break open.

The software has to run for the length of an exhibition. Some material is never shown.

## Context

Developed during Con.Divisione 12 Art Residency in 2023.
highlights: Net-art system that inserts misleading edits into unspecified Wikipedia articles as a continuous stream of altered text
Residency: Con.Divisione 12 Art Residency (2023)

projects.title: Fonema
projects.description:
## Overview

Fonema is an audio installation about artificial intelligence and human communication. Recorded voices pass through an artificial neural network. What comes back still sounds like speech in grain and rhythm, but sentences do not hold: enough to suggest a person, not enough to settle on a meaning.

It uses voice-classification and recognition-style models. The output is tuned to break lexical meaning, not to label speakers or transcribe speech.
projects.descriptionAfterVideos:
## How it works

The work looks at neural architectures and audio signal-processing chains: how latent spaces and decision boundaries behave when you stop asking the model to label cleanly and keep it between word and noise. The voices can feel like overhearing a conversation you are not following.

In the installation, the focus is on how machine-mediated audio shapes whether spoken language feels trustworthy.

## Context

Fonema was a thesis project. Research, prototyping, and the installation form came out of that academic frame, not a commission.
highlights: Installation that routes speech through a neural network so timbre stays familiar while lexical meaning slips
Models associated with voice classification and recognition, used toward unstable listening instead of labelling
